subject: Four-way close synchronization: MAP re-baseline and risk ledger
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@helixhealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Four-way close synchronization: MAP re-baseline and risk ledger

Hi Ava / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We walked through the remaining eval gates and the procurement cadence; from Redwood's side the blockers we heard are: SOC2 evidence for our private tunnel, a short PoC validation window for your API integration, and procurement legal needing redlines on the SLA appendix.

Attached is a proposed MAP (v3) that staggers acceptance:
- Phase 1 (PoC): limited traffic + success criteria (5 business days)
- Phase 2 (Eval): expanded test set + eval results & regression checks (10 business days)
- Phase 3 (Full go-live): SLA and retention commitments signed

If Helix agrees to the staggered acceptance approach we can keep the overall close window but shift the hard go-live date by +7 business days to give procurement and legal time to run redlines without blocking the PoC. That change reduces risk of a full slip while preserving the evaluation gating you requested.

Request: please confirm by EOD whether you can sign off on the staggered MAP. I’ve included Laura and Ben from the engagement team so we can update the risk ledger and plan fallback capacity.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2_evidence_request.pdf (document stub)

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@helixhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@helixhealth.com>, procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Four-way close synchronization: MAP re-baseline and risk ledger

Jonas —

Thanks for the summary and the MAP draft. High level: Helix is aligned with a phased acceptance, but we do need:
1) SOC2 artifacts and an evidence checklist before Phase 2 (Legal will not greenlight retention terms without this).
2) A short technical success criteria doc for the PoC (we want specific latency / error rate thresholds).
3) Procurement will need the SLA appendix redlined — they asked to see the proposed language today so they can slot review into their Tuesday meeting.

I’ve looped procurement (procurement@helixhealth.com) — Samir and I will push to get legal time, but if Redwood can commit to the +7 business day buffer that would be helpful.

We’ll review the MAP internally and send a single consolidated response by Tuesday morning.

—Ava
Ava Collins
Director, Digital Platforms | HelixHealth
ava.collins@helixhealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@helixhealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Four-way close synchronization: MAP re-baseline and risk ledger

Ava — thank you. Quick responses inline and a proposed operational fallback: 

- SOC2 artifacts: Laura has the checklist and we can deliver a scoping pack by EOD tomorrow (will include encryption in transit details, retention windows, and audit log samples).
- PoC success criteria: Ben will draft an explicit test matrix with thresholds (latency < 350ms P95, error rate < 0.5% on test corpus).
- SLA appendix redlines: We’ll prepare suggested language and a comment-ready doc for your legal team Monday night.

Operational fallback (risk ledger entry): If legal cannot clear the SLA by the new go-live deadline, we propose running the production cutover as a restricted pilot for a single business unit (scope limited to 20% traffic) while legal finishes final sign-off. That keeps product momentum while protecting both sides.

If Helix confirms the +7 business day buffer and agrees to the pilot fallback, we’ll update the MAP and post it to the HubSpot record (link below).

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/HLX-2027-045

Cheers,
Jonas

Jonas / team — quick note from solutions:

I reviewed the MAP v3 and the proposed PoC thresholds. Two tactical asks before we send final language:
- Add an automated regression checklist that runs after each PoC day (we can provide a CI job that posts a pass/fail summary to the shared folder).
- Add a temporary throttling policy for Phase 1 (so Helix can ramp up without impacting production SLA).

Also, recommend we carve out a canary rollback window in the MAP: 24 hours post-phase acceptance where we can reverse the cut if we hit unseen regressions. That should be acceptable to procurement and reduces the legal appetite for longer retention guarantees.

Putting Ben on the PoC criteria doc; Laura, can you confirm SOC2 artifact ETA and whether we need a signed NDA supplement for audit logs?

Thanks — I’ll stand by to update the MAP spreadsheet.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 10:54:00 -0700
Subject: Helix — procurement review: SLA appendix and audit evidence needs

Jonas / Jonas team —

Helix procurement reviewed the MAP and has two items that will hold legal until addressed:
1) Appendix A (SLA): Clarify data retention windows and provide a binding exception process for access requests.
2) Audit evidence: we need retention proof for audit logs and a contact at Redwood who can respond to an external compliance request within 48 hours.

We can proceed with the PoC while legal reviews but will not sign full go-live until items above are resolved. I’m attaching our review notes—please respond with markups.

Attachment: Helix_review_notes.pdf (review stub)

Procurement Team
HelixHealth

Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation summary & ask: buffer approval and executive sync

Team / Helix execs —

Summary of current risk posture: Helix procurement needs Appendix A clarifications and binding retention language; legal is likely to push a 5–7 business day review. To avoid a full close slip we’ve proposed a +7 business day buffer with a restricted pilot fallback (20% traffic) and a 24-hour canary rollback window. Helix procurement has agreed to allow the PoC to proceed while legal reviews.

Ask (Redwood leadership): please approve a discretionary buffer of up to 7 business days on the HLX-2027-045 close date and authorize an executive intro between Redwood's Head of Legal and HelixHealth's counsel if needed. This will let us keep momentum, preserve the evaluation cadence, and reduce the likelihood of a multi-week delay.

I’ve attached the updated MAP (Redwood_MAP_v3.xlsx) and Helix’s review notes. If leadership approves, I’ll schedule a 30-minute exec sync for Monday to unblock legal.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
